The President's Cake | Arthouse Now — Sun Oct 25, 4:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
While people struggle daily to survive under sanctions in Saddam’s Iraq, nine-year-old Lamia must use her wits to gather ingredients for the mandatory cake to celebrate President Saddam Hussein’s birthday or face the consequences—prison or death. A touching coming-of-age tale that combines empathy, pragmatism, universally relatable characters, and striking cinematography. [105 min; drama; Arabic with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: An Evening With Wright Thompson & Michael Koryta — Sun Oct 25, 5:00 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description:
BLOOMINGTON BOOK FEST: WRIGHT THOMPSON Join the Bloomington Book Festival for the third annual presentation of the Bob Hammel Writing Award.
The 2026 winner and keynote speaker is Wright Thompson, a New York Times-bestselling author and revered journalist. A native of Clarksdale, in the Mississippi Delta, Thompson has spent two decades proving that the best stories are often about ambition, loss, family, and the price of greatness.
His latest book, The Barn: The Secret History of a Murder in Mississippi, is a haunting account of the brutal 1955 murder of Emmett Till, named a Best Book of the Year by the Washington Post, TIME, and Vanity Fair, and nominated for a PEN America Literary Award.

item.title: Kagemusha | Michael A. McRobbie's Choice — Sun Oct 25, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Akira Kurosawa's lauded feudal epic follows the story of a petty thief recruited to impersonate an aging warlord in an effort to keep the warlord safe from attacking competing clans. When the warlord dies, his general reluctantly empowers the imposter to take over as the ruler to maintain their control. But his commitment to his new role is tested when forced to lead “his” troops into battle. Winner of the 1980 Cannes Film Festival Palme d’Or, Kagemusha merges the passion of youthful artistic creation with the genius of a master filmmaker. [162 min; drama, war; Japanese with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop — Mon Oct 26, 6:00 PM — Global & International Studies Building
item.description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.
It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.
Instructions:
Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session
If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop.
If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.

item.title: Open Gate Day at Bradford Woods — Sat Nov 14 — Bradford Woods
item.description:
Bradford Woods will host an Open Gate Day on November 14! Stop by between 10 am and 2 pm for a fun day in the outdoors with free fishing, ziplining, rope climbing, archery, and hiking! Pack a picnic and enjoy lunch on the property, too. Here are a few important details: Ziplining and climbing participants must weigh at least 50 lbs. Anyone age 18 or older who plans to fish must have a valid Indiana fishing license. Please bring your own bait and tackle. Fishing is land-based only.
Source: Visit Morgan County

item.title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building — Sat Nov 14, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup Would you like to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar. Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30. Meet at the parking lot at the base of Gose Creek Road at the end of Hinson Road in Martinsville. Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)
Source: Knobsto
